title: Chapter V

teacherSummary.text: Gatsby has Nick's lawn cut and fills his cottage with flowers. The reunion begins in painful awkwardness, then after half an hour Daisy and Gatsby are radiant. Gatsby shows Daisy his mansion and throws his shirts before her; she sobs. He mentions the green light at the end of her dock. Klipspringer plays the piano. Nick leaves them together, sensing that Daisy cannot match Gatsby's dream.

segments.activity: Model the close reading of the anchor quotation using the written think-aloud below.
segments.script: First, meaning. I read “They’re such beautiful shirts” slowly and put it in my own words: Daisy cries over Gatsby's shirts, saying they are so beautiful. Next, craft. I notice how strange it is: she weeps over clothing, not over Gatsby himself. The strongest word is “beautiful”: it is a vague word that shows she is moved by beauty and wealth. Then, effect. What does Daisy's response to the shirts show? My answer: Daisy is overwhelmed by what Gatsby's money shows; her tears suggest she is moved by his wealth and by what she lost, and hint that she values things.
